prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas. Injury: neck and back strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1490; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my name on this recording, so just call me the plaintiff.

Q: Understood. Where were you on the day of the collision?
A: I was driving north on a two-lane road in Conroe, Texas, heading home from the grocery store.

Q: What happened next?
A: A vehicle coming the other way drifted across the center line. I braked and steered right, but we still made contact. It was a head-on collision, though honestly it didn't feel like a high-speed impact. We both had maybe a few miles an hour left when we touched.

Q: Did your airbags deploy?
A: No, they didn't. My car jolted forward and back, and my head snapped a bit. That's what I remember most.

Q: Did you feel pain right away?
A: Not immediately. I felt a little stiff in the neck and a dull ache in my lower back within an hour or so. By that evening it was harder to turn my head to check mirrors.

Q: Did you seek medical care?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that same week. They diagnosed a neck strain and a lumbar strain and gave me muscle relaxers and a referral to physical therapy.

Q: Have you attended physical therapy?
A: I went about twice a week for several weeks. The exercises help some days more than others. I still do the home stretches they showed me.

Q: How has this affected your daily life?
A: I used to coach my nephew's soccer team on weekends, and I had to hand that off to my brother for a while. Lifting groceries is uncomfortable, and I've been sleeping in a recliner some nights because lying flat hurts my back.

Q: Are you working currently?
A: Yes, I'm back at my desk job. I take short breaks to stand up and stretch, and my supervisor has been accommodating about that.

Q: Do you have any prior neck or back complaints?
A: Nothing serious. I had a stiff neck now and then from sitting at a computer, but nothing that needed a doctor.
